title: BioNTech’s mRNA cancer vaccine fails phase 3 test, significantly denting analysts’ confidence
summary: A phase 2/3 clinical trial of BioNTech’s mRNA cancer immunotherapy BNT113 has missed one of its dual primary endpoints. But with immature overall survival data offering a path to redemption, the German biotech is continuing to track patients in the metastatic head and neck cancer study.

title: Biotech builder Paragon imports Apogee's top brass after AbbVie buyout
summary: It’s been a busy morning for Paragon Labs. In addition to bringing over much of the leadership team from AbbVie-acquired Apogee Therapeutics, Paragon has overseen a reverse merger to take its hypertension-focused spinout Velaris Therapeutics public.

title: Roche inks $1.2B deal with China's Rona to enter emerging ALK7 obesity race
summary: Roche has committed $100 million in upfront and near-term payments to license Rona Therapeutics’ ALK7 drug candidate, joining Alnylam, Arrowhead, GSK and Novo Nordisk in an emerging obesity niche.

title: Pfizer inks $500M Enodia pact to join Lilly in emerging protein degrader field
summary: Pfizer has followed Eli Lilly into the Sec61 space, inking a $500 million deal with Enodia Therapeutics days after its Big Pharma peer formed an $870 million pact with Gate Bioscience.

title: Nurix drops one BTK degrader as momentum builds behind Roche-partnered option
summary: Nurix’s BTK degrader zelebrudomide may have survived a clinical hold in recent years, but that hasn’t stopped the California biotech from dropping the cancer drug.

title: Roche sets sights on FDA approval decision of July 2027 with updated eye drug data
summary: One year on from a mixed phase 3 readout, Roche has shared updated data from eye disease trials that could support FDA approval by July.

title: Tortugas’ schizophrenia drug proves worth in phase 2 Hansoh trial in China
summary: Tortugas Neuroscience’s schizophrenia drug from Hansoh Pharma has proven its worth in a phase 2b study, validating the fledgling biotech’s neurology strategy.

title: BMS doubles up with pivotal wins in lung disease, solid tumor that offer hope for post-patent cliff growth

title: iRegene Therapeutics’s NouvSight001 Cleared for Clinical Trials in the U.S. and China for Retinitis Pigmentosa

title: Merck’s deeper dive into efficacy, safety of $1.3B eye disease drug raises fears of ‘limited’ potential
summary: Merck & Co. has poured out its Brunello data, revealing a mix of undifferentiated efficacy and concerning safety that led analysts to predict “limited competitive potential” in diabetic macular edema. The company paid $1.3 billion upfront in 2024 to buy the asset and the rest of Eyebiotech.

title: Chutes & Ladders—Vir looks to Liu to lead late-stage push

title: Microglia Rescue Vulnerable Dopamine Neurons in Parkinson’s
summary: Summary: Researchers at the University of Oxford have discovered that human microglia can selectively prune away toxic alpha-synuclein aggregates from dopamine-producing neurons without destroying the host nerve cells. Utilizing co-cultures of human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived neurons and microglia, the team demonstrated that microglia employ “trogocytosis”, a precise cellular nibbling mechanism, regulated by GPNMB, P2RY12, and CD22 signaling pathways, along with an IL-10 molecular brake. The findings identify a distinct, neuroprotective microglial subtype that shields neurons in Parkinson’s disease. […]

title: Alus harbor genetic variants that shape the human cortex
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02492-wThe genetic changes associated with development of the human cortex are difficult to test functionally, especially in the context of gene regulation. In this issue, Matoba et al. show that variants that shape human cortical structure are hiding inside Alu transposable elements, co-opting their inbuilt machinery to rewire regulatory networks in the developing brain.

title: Investigating molecular and hemodynamic effects of LSD in the human brain

title: Genome-wide analysis of common structural variants in Alzheimer’s disease identifies a risk-associated regulatory CCG repeat in FAM193B
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02481-zThis study identifies common structural variants contributing to Alzheimer’s disease heritability. An expanded promoter CCG repeat increases FAM193B expression and disease risk, linking its expression to DNA damage and cell death pathways in neurons.

title: Alzheimer’s disease target and drug discovery by leveraging multiomics and electronic health data

title: Modality-specific reactive and predictive responses in the human superior colliculus

title: Astrocytes regulate axonal mitochondrial transport deficits in C9ORF72 amyotrophic lateral sclerosis motor neurons
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02464-0Astrocytes regulate axonal mitochondrial transport in motor neurons through mitochondrial bioenergetics, a process disrupted in C9ORF72-mediated amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
